subject: 9mmhandgun
leg: control: Valve's own against the brief
label: 9mmhandgun, in the place of the game's models/v_9mmhandgun.mdl, models/p_9mmhandgun.mdl, models/w_9mmhandgun.mdl

measured.lineup: the asset is one of A to D in lineup.png beside models/w_grenade.mdl, models/w_satchel.mdl, models/w_357.mdl
measured.lineupTest: asked 4 times, each in another order, which of the four was not made by Valve: judges picked A, A, D, D where the asset was B, D, A, B: passed for one of the game's

M1.reason: Read against the brief (a 9mm pistol lying on its side), the outline is a pistol: a long slide with the rear serrations and the muzzle at its ends (top view), a grip block sticking out sideways (top and below views), and a trigger guard loop (below view). The thin dimension is vertical in the side views, so it lies flat as asked. Nothing sticks out or is missing in the outline.

M2.reason: Measured length 9.5 to 9.7 units against the brief's 10, a 0.028 difference, well within 15%. Width 1.9 and height 9.7 are what a pistol lying on its side should measure.

M3.reason: Parts the brief implies, checked down to the small ones. Present: slide, muzzle bore (back view, round hole), serrations at the rear of the slide (top view, y 280 to 330), a rear sight bracket (top view, x 1690 to 1740), trigger guard and trigger (below view, x 150 to 205, y 530 to 605), grip. Missing: no front sight is visible at the muzzle end in the top, front or front-left views, and no magazine base is distinct at the bottom of the grip. A small part missing caps M3 at 1.

M4.reason: Black polymer grip and dark grey steel slide, as the brief asks. The first-person view and the in-hand picture show the same dark finish with lighter steel on the slide. No region is a wrong colour.

M5.reason: The brief asks for no markings, so the surface needs only to be plain. In in-hand.png the slide's texture runs in long light streaks along its length that read as a stretched or smeared texture, not steel. That is a painted fault, charged here to M5, not to shape.

M6.reason: Capped at 2 by the line-up measure: the line-up of four (A is the asset) was not picked as the one Valve did not make in any of the four readings, so a player would take it for one of the game's.

M7.reason: Lying on its side as the brief asks: the thin 1.9 axis is vertical, the grip points sideways, and the muzzle is at the end opposite the rear serrations. The origin placement is not measured here and nothing in the pictures shows it floating or sunk.

M8.reason: SMAK's check reports no errors. 88 triangles is under the median of 142 for Half-Life's own props of this kind and size. The views show no open faces: the bore at the muzzle is a recess a player sees, not a hole in the shell.

W1.reason: In first-person.png the asset sits in the hand where the game's own handgun sits, the same way round, with the muzzle up and the grip in the palm. Through the 14 attack frames in attack.png the pistol stays in the hand and only kicks up and rotates with the recoil. It never parts from the hand where both are seen.
